summary: Ship signature-reference readers before the storage-format cutover; default stores remain version 20 with inline signature text

replay.detail: No claim replay is required. Installing the reader does not convert default v20 signature relationships. The later v21 converter uses local stored evidence, preserving canonical text, lexical candidate ordering, global nonce evidence and conflict semantics.

schema.detail: Default storage identity remains 20. Empty claim_signature_originals and claim_signature_reference_migration tables are additive, local representation infrastructure; no history is converted in default v20 stores. Reader compatibility additionally accepts version21 without lowering its marker. Within explicitly activated v21 fixtures, sources, the selected-signature facade and judging cursors use32-byte SHA-256 references to exact original text. Canonical candidate text and PRIMARY KEY(claim_id,signature) ordering remain unchanged. This release does not activate production compaction or claim default-store byte savings.

rules.detail: Signature verification, canonical candidate selection and global nonce admission rules do not change. A reference does not replace the original signed text as evidence.

compatibility.detail: Reader-first rollout: default v20 writers retain inline TEXT readable by the previous published release. This binary also reads and writes reference-bearing v21 stores without relabeling them as v20. Only a later release whose published N-1 already has this reader may flip the default writer format. Signed claim bytes, peer wire formats and authorization semantics are unchanged.

downtime.detail: Default v20 stores install empty additive tables but do not scan or compact signature history. Explicitly activated v21 fixtures exercise online conversion after authorization bootstrap, at most64 rows per advance with a10ms cooperative budget checked between rows. Individual SQLite operations and commit can exceed that budget. No whole-store conversion transaction or history-sized index build runs.

manual.detail: No manual action is required. Do not change user_version to activate compaction. Reader publication and a later format-flip release are required before production byte reduction is enabled.

recovery.detail: Default v20 stores retain previous-release reopen/write/rollback compatibility. A v21 store is never silently relabeled as20. Future v21 activation requires an N-1 reader with v21 support; its bounded converter preserves original text, checkpoints each page atomically and resumes without discarding candidate or nonce evidence.
